content.user_title: Craft EVP Messaging for Your Audience Awareness Tier
content.value_statement: Generic value propositions can miss the pain and awareness level of a specific audience. This skill drafts three concise alternatives and checks their specificity and fit.
actual_capabilities: Collect an awareness tier, customer segment, prospect pain, specific outcome, tradeoff, and optional proof.
Generate three variants with outcome-led, tradeoff-led, and customer-profile-led emphasis.
Review each variant for a maximum of 22 words, specificity, customer fit, pain vocabulary, and awareness alignment.
Recommend a primary variant with a one-sentence rationale.
Suggest message placements and identify supporting proof for the selected tier.
Critique an existing EVP with word count, tier fit, issues, and a rewrite in the same voice.
limitations: This is an internal sub-skill loaded by the parent evp skill, not a directly invocable standalone command.
The referenced parent framework is not included in the reviewed package.
The skill relies on supplied pain, outcomes, and proof; it does not independently research or verify them.
Word counts and message checks are model self-checks, not executable validation or evidence of conversion performance.

use_cases.title: Develop segment-specific positioning
use_cases.description: Compare three EVP angles for a defined customer segment and one awareness tier before selecting a primary message.

use_cases.title: Prepare prospect conversation openers
use_cases.description: Draft concise sales openers using prospect pain, a concrete outcome, and a specific tradeoff.

use_cases.title: Review page messaging
use_cases.description: Critique an existing headline or tagline for word count, audience fit, and specificity, then rewrite it in the same voice.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an awareness tier
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a Schwartz awareness tier for [audience]. They describe their problem as [pain] and currently know [solutions or products]. Ask for missing details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: clarify the audience before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Draft three EVP variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft three EVP variants for tier [1-5]. ICP: [segment]. Pain: [prospect wording]. Outcome: [specific result]. Tradeoff: [avoided cost]. Proof: [optional evidence]. Keep each within 22 words.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: produce alternatives from a complete brief.

prompt_templates.title: Critique an existing EVP
prompt_templates.prompt: Critique this EVP: [text]. Intended audience: [segment]. Intended tier: [1-5]. Report word count, actual tier fit, and specific issues. Rewrite it in the same voice.

prompt_templates.title: Select a primary message
prompt_templates.prompt: For tier [1-5], generate three variants using [ICP], [pain], [outcome], [tradeoff], and [proof]. Check every criterion, recommend a primary, and explain suitable placements. Identify unsupported claims without inventing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare messages and prepare a publication review.

output_examples.input: Draft a Tier 3 EVP for agency owners facing unpredictable pipelines. Outcome: 14 qualified meetings monthly. Tradeoff: hiring more sales representatives.
output: Outcome-led: For agency owners facing unpredictable pipelines, we deliver 14 qualified meetings monthly without hiring more sales representatives.
Tradeoff-led: For agency owners facing unpredictable pipelines, we deliver 14 qualified meetings monthly without adding sales headcount.
ICP-led: Agency owners with unpredictable pipelines use us for 14 qualified meetings monthly without hiring more sales representatives.
Recommended primary: Outcome-led, because the supplied meeting target makes the result concrete.
Proof needed: Evidence supporting the supplied monthly meeting target.

output_examples.input: Critique this EVP for agency owners at Tier 3: We help businesses grow faster with innovative solutions.
output: Tier-fit: Unclear; the line does not name a solution or define the audience.
Issues: The audience is broad, the outcome is unmeasured, and the tradeoff is missing.
Rewrite requires: A concrete outcome, the prospect pain wording, and an avoided tradeoff.
Next question: What measurable result can you substantiate for agency owners?

best_practices: Use prospect language for pain and name a customer segment that excludes poor-fit audiences.
Provide a concrete outcome and supporting evidence before selecting copy for publication.
Review every variant against the 22-word limit, specific tradeoffs, and the selected awareness tier.
anti_patterns: Drafting an EVP without a clear prospect pain statement.
Replacing concrete outcomes with vague claims such as improve or grow.
Using product-aware messaging for an audience that only recognizes its problem.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It drafts three EVP variants for one awareness tier, recommends a primary, and suggests placements and supporting proof.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the awareness tier, specific customer segment, prospect pain, concrete outcome, and avoided tradeoff. Supporting proof is optional.

faq.question: Must each variant contain exactly 22 words?
faq.answer: No. The validation table specifies a maximum of 22 words for each variant.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing EVP?
faq.answer: Yes. The critique workflow reports word count, tier fit, and issues, then requests a rewrite in the original voice.

faq.question: Can I invoke evp-craft directly?
faq.answer: The skill declares itself non-user-invocable. The parent evp skill loads it for tier-specific drafting requests.

faq.question: Does it verify outcomes or proof?
faq.answer: No. It uses supplied information and requests aligned proof, but it does not independently validate claims or guarantee conversion results.
